newsitem.title: UK: Unions, UPS dispute "day of action" impact.
newsitem.headline: Unions, UPS dispute "day of action" impact.

text.p: Union and company officials disputed the impact in Europe of Thursday's "day of action" against United Parcel Service of America.

Union sources said today's action largely consisted of brief stoppages, leaflet distribution and information meetings by UPS European staff as well as at the company's U.S. headquarters in Atlanta and in Brazil.
A UPS statement from its European headquarters said the action was hardly supported by any employees, and added that none of the company's domestic or international services were affected.
However a spokesman for the day's organisers International Transport Workers Federation (ITF)told Reuters:"We are pleased with the response and we feel it has been a success".
"Our intention was not to disrupt UPS activities but to demonstrate support for the World UPS Trade Council (formed in London this February)."

The council was setup to try and achieve a coordinated approach to UPS over working conditions. It is concerned at UPS' apparent moves towards using more sub-contractors and owner-drivers, the trend towards more part-time jobs and the need for work place safety.
In Germany, the country's OeTV transport union, said 1,000 out of 14,000 UPS workers were took part. Other countries involved were France, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain and Belgium.
There was also a small demonstration outside the UPS European headquarters in Brussels with representatives from unions in most of the countries involved, including the U.S.-based Teamsters union.
The latter's four-year UPS contract is due for renegotiation in July and today's company statement said "The day of action was... to put pressure on UPS for the forthcoming negotiations."
Separately the ITF World Council is planning a meeting during June in Washington D.C. to discuss the need for a UPS code of conduct towards its workers.
UPS Italy also said today that a scheduled meeting with local union representatives will still take place on May 28.

There have been several strikes and other forms of action by UPS Italia staff since the company announced 150 layoff out of 900 staff in early March, an industry source said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
